questions.prompt: Explain the difference between offset-limit pagination and cursor-based pagination. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that offset-limit pagination uses page numbers or skip counts, which can produce duplicates when new items are added
Explains that cursor pagination uses an opaque pointer to the last item, preventing duplicate shifts and performing faster on large datasets

questions.modelAnswer: Offset-limit pagination requests data using a page number or skip count, allowing arbitrary page jumping. However, if new records are inserted at the top of a feed while scrolling, existing items shift down and create duplicate rows on subsequent pages. In contrast, cursor-based pagination uses an opaque pointer to the last viewed record, preventing duplicate shifts and improving database index performance.

questions.prompt: Why should infinite scrolling trigger a few items before the end of a list rather than on the last item? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that triggering on the last item forces the user to wait for network latency and loading spinners
Explains that triggering on a threshold item prefetches content in the background, creating a continuous scroll experience

questions.modelAnswer: Triggering pagination only when the user reaches the final row forces them to stop scrolling and wait for network latency. By triggering a prefetch five or ten items before the end, the next page downloads silently in the background while the user continues viewing content. This eliminates loading delays and creates a seamless, uninterrupted infinite scrolling experience.

questions.prompt: How do you prevent duplicate network requests when users scroll quickly past pagination threshold items? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that rapid scrolling can trigger onAppear multiple times in quick succession
Explains using an isLoading boolean guard or task cancellation before starting a network fetch

questions.modelAnswer: When a user flings a scroll view, multiple rows near the threshold trigger their onAppear closures within milliseconds. To prevent launching duplicate network calls for the same page, developers should guard the fetch method with a boolean isLoading check. When isLoading is true, subsequent trigger calls return immediately until the inflight request completes.

questions.prompt: Why must paginated items be deduplicated before appending to a SwiftUI collection? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that SwiftUI ForEach requires unique, stable identifiers to perform view diffing
Explains that duplicate IDs cause layout glitches, animation failures, or runtime crashes

questions.modelAnswer: SwiftUI ForEach containers require stable and unique identifiers for every child view to manage view identity and animations. If network retries or concurrent calls append items with duplicate IDs, SwiftUI diffing algorithms fail. This causes visual glitches, broken animations, or runtime layout crashes, which deduplicating by ID prevents.

questions.prompt: Describe how to properly handle pull-to-refresh on a paginated feed without corrupting existing list state. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains resetting pagination state by clearing items, setting cursor to nil, and setting hasMore to true
Explains fetching page one fresh so new items replace rather than awkwardly append to old batches

questions.modelAnswer: When a user triggers pull-to-refresh, the app must reset its pagination state rather than appending newly fetched items to the end of the existing array. The ViewModel should cancel inflight pagination tasks, reset the nextCursor to nil, and set hasMore to true. It then fetches page one fresh and replaces the existing array, ensuring correct chronological order without duplicate rows.
